meta.reference_vehicle: BMW M3 Competition Sedan (G80), rear-wheel drive, 8-speed M Steptronic, model years 2021-2024 (pre-2024-LCI focus)
meta.purpose: Engineering reference for a fictional car in Redline Highway. Real names appear only in docs.

tags.M: measured in a magazine or independent test

meta.units_note: SI unless a unit says otherwise. Imperial magazine figures are kept as published and converted in notes.
meta.research_limits: The team's shared web-search budget ran out near the end of this session, so the video list and a few gaps could not be searched further.

chassis_code.note: G81 = Touring, G82/G83 = M4 Coupe/Convertible share the drivetrain.

type_codes.note: Fitment table lists 31AY and 32AY as G80 M3 Competition (11/2020-06/2024); a Japanese homologation photo title '3BA-32AY30 M3 Competition M xDrive' on Commons suggests 32AY = M xDrive.

engine_code.note: T0 = Competition output; base M3 is S58B30O0. ADAC lists S58B30A for the 07/22-05/24 car.

production_and_years.value: Launch March 2021; M xDrive from summer 2021 (US MY2022); running update 07/2022; LCI from 07/2024
production_and_years.note: 07/2022 and 07/2024 dates from ADAC catalogue periods. LCI raised the M xDrive to 390 kW/530 PS; RWD Competition stayed at 375 kW/510 PS (ADAC, Wikipedia).

body.value: 4-door, 5-seat notchback sedan with standard CFRP roof

trim_researched.value: M3 Competition Sedan, rear-wheel drive, 8-speed M Steptronic with Drivelogic

us_vs_eu_power.value: Identical engine: 375 kW = 510 PS (EU) = 503 hp SAE (US). Only the units differ.

us_vs_eu_mass.value: EU DIN 1,730 kg (no driver, 90% fuel); EU 1,805 kg (DIN + 75 kg driver/luggage); US curb 3,890 lb = 1,764 kg (full fuel, no driver)

us_vs_eu_other.value: EU/RoW cars carry gasoline particulate filters (OPF) in the exhaust; US cars do not. 2021 US spec lists 18/19-inch wheels as standard and 19/20-inch optional; most test cars ran 19/20.
us_vs_eu_other.note: OPF note: ST1926 marks the underbody catalytic converter/particulate filter 'Not for the US' (F97 manual, same S58 exhaust concept); vendors confirm for G80 (OPF_VENDORS).

m_xdrive_differences.value: Transfer case with electronically controlled multi-plate clutch, rear-only in normal driving; modes 4WD, 4WD Sport, 2WD (DSC off). +50 kg DIN (about +100 lb US). Steering ratio 14.6:1 vs 15.0:1. Standard 19/20-inch wheels. 0-100 km/h 3.5 s (vs 3.9), 0-60 mph 3.4 s (vs 3.8). From 07/2024 (LCI) 390 kW/530 PS.
m_xdrive_differences.note: Mass delta from BMW regional pages (1,780 kg DIN xDrive) and US curb 3,990 vs 3,890 lb.

layout.note: 'vorne / laengs' in AMS data; BMW: in-line 6.

block.value: Aluminium closed-deck crankcase without liners; wire-arc-sprayed iron bore coating

head.value: Aluminium; 3D-printed sand core for coolant passages

crankshaft.value: Forged lightweight steel crank (42CrMoS4 mod, nitrocarburised), approx. 21.2 kg
crankshaft.note: Throw layout for an even-firing inline-6 is 120 deg (A).

valvetrain.value: DOHC, 4 valves/cylinder, chain-driven cams, VALVETRONIC fully variable valve lift, Double-VANOS

fuel_system.value: High Precision direct injection, 350 bar max

max_power_rpm.note: BMW's own output diagram shows a flat 375 kW plateau from 5,600 to 7,200 rpm (BMW_SPEC_M4), so treat 6,250 as a point on that plateau.

torque_curve_crank_factory.note: Read from BMW's full-load diagram (M4 spec sheet, labelled '375 KW @ 5600-7200 rpm' and '650 Nm @ 2750-5500 rpm'; same engine and tune as M3 Competition). The diagram is vector art, so the vertices were extracted from the PDF drawing commands rather than eyeballed; accuracy about +/-1 Nm. Above 5,500 rpm torque equals 375 kW / omega. This is BMW's nominal (stylised) curve, not a dyno trace.

torque_curve_crank_500rpm_steps.note: Same source as above, sampled at 500 rpm steps; 7,200 rpm is the end of BMW's curve (redline).

power_curve_crank_factory.note: Extracted from the same vector diagram.

torque_curve_wheel_dyno_measured.note: Stock 2022 M4 Competition xDrive (same S58B30T0 + 8HP76; AWD drivetrain), Mustang dynamometer, 93 octane US pump fuel, SAE-type weather correction. Read from the published chart image by pixel digitising (consistency check: hp computed from the torque trace matches the plotted hp within 1-2 hp). Original units 338-443 lb-ft. Peak 443 lb-ft (601 Nm) near 3,000-3,500 rpm and 449 whp (335 kW) near 5,800 rpm. Mustang dynos read lower than Dynojets.

underrating_note.value: Measured wheel power (335 kW at the wheels on a conservative Mustang dyno, AWD) implies roughly 385-400 kW at the crank with 13-16% losses, i.e. the 375 kW rating is conservative.
underrating_note.note: Supporting: MotorTrend says 'BMW historically has underrated its beefier engines' (MT_XD); a base manual M3 dynoed at about 496 hp vs 473 rated (BMWBLOG_DYNO). Loss assumption is an estimate.

limiter_rpm.note: evo: 'the limiter coming in at 7250rpm'. In M (manual) mode the gearbox does not upshift at the limiter (BMW_PK).

design_rated_speed.note: Training manual: pistons and Valvetronic designed for a rated engine speed of 7,500 rpm. Not the road-car limiter.

idle_rpm.note: Not found. Typical warm idle for BMW B58/S58 automatics is about 650-750 rpm; cold-start flare about 1,200-1,500 rpm for a few seconds (BMW_ST1926 notes a catalyst-heating mode for ~30 s after start). Verify against a video.

launch_control_rpm.note: Secondary, generic source: 'M Steptronic holds engine revolutions around 2,700 rpm'. The Citizen: launch flag appears after about 2 s of building boost to around 1.0 bar, and the RWD car launches in 2nd gear (CITIZEN_ART). C/D xDrive: 'boost holding above 15.0 psi' at launch (CD_XD). Treat 2,500-3,000 rpm as the plausible range.

engine_mass.note: Not published. Wikipedia gives 139 kg dry for the single-turbo B58 (uncited). The S58 adds a second turbo/manifold, forged internals and a larger oil system: estimate 160-175 kg dry, about 190 kg with fluids, turbos and ancillaries.

rotating_inertia.note: Not published. Estimate for crank, rods, pistons, damper, flexplate plus torque-converter impeller side. Crank alone 21.2 kg (F).

firing_order.note: Standard for BMW inline-sixes (M20 through N55/S54 in BMW training material). Not stated in any S58-specific document I opened; strongly expected (A).

cylinder_numbering.value: Cylinder 1 at the front (belt/pulley end), cylinder 6 at the rear (gearbox end). Front turbo/manifold serves cylinders 1-3, rear turbo serves 4-6.
cylinder_numbering.note: Bank grouping is F (BMW_PK, BMW_ST1926); 1-at-front is the BMW convention (FIRING).

firing_interval_and_frequency.value: 120 deg crank between firings; firing frequency = rpm / 20 Hz (35 Hz at 700 rpm, 125 Hz at 2,500, 360 Hz at 7,200). With 1-5-3-6-2-4, each turbo/exhaust branch receives evenly spaced pulses every 240 deg (1.5th order per branch).
firing_interval_and_frequency.note: Arithmetic for a 4-stroke inline-6: 3 firings per revolution.

type.value: Twin-turbo, two mono-scroll (single-scroll) turbochargers, one per 3-cylinder bank
type.note: Press kit: 'two mono-scroll turbochargers, which supply compressed air to cylinders 1-3 and 4-6 respectively'.

maker.note: 'The system supplier for the mono-scroll turbocharger assembly on the S58 engine is the MHI Group.' Retailers sell OEM Mitsubishi units, BMW part nos. 11658469097 (bank 1) and 11658469098 (bank 2) (TURNER_TURBO).

model.note: Turbo frame/model and wheel sizes not published. Gap.

twin_scroll.note: Mono-scroll; each turbine housing is cast together with its 3-into-1 exhaust manifold.

max_boost.note: AMS lists 'max. Ladedruck 1,7 bar'. C/D: 24.7 psi (1.70 bar) for Competition vs 18.9 psi (1.30 bar) for the base M3 (CD_RWD). Both read as gauge pressure.

boost_build_rpm.value: Torque climbs from 345 Nm at 2,000 rpm to 460 Nm at 2,500 and reaches 650 Nm at about 2,750 rpm
boost_build_rpm.note: Measured wheel dyno: plateau from about 2,900-3,000 rpm (ARM_DYNO). Reviewers note noticeable lag below that (CD_COMP, CITIZEN_ART).

wastegate.value: Electric wastegate actuator per turbo, PWM-controlled by the DME; fast closing for response, can open fully to heat the catalysts

blow_off_behaviour.value: No atmospheric blow-off valve is documented; stock cars make no audible 'pssh'. Any compressor recirculation is internal.
blow_off_behaviour.note: Assumption based on absence in BMW documents and on BMW practice; a faint turbo whoosh/flutter on lift-off is plausible but unverified.

intercooling.value: Indirect (air-to-liquid) charge-air cooling in the intake plenum, low-temperature circuit with electric pump

type.value: 8-speed M Steptronic with Drivelogic, torque-converter automatic

model.note: US spec table names 'M8HP76'; parts sellers list 8HP76 for G80 M3 Competition (TURNER_8HP76, LEEBMANN_TC). C/D and MT call it ZF-sourced.

final_drive.note: US sheet rounds to 3.15. Overall top gear 2.02:1 (MT_COMP).

speed_at_7200rpm_by_gear.note: Rolling radius 0.335 m (285/30 ZR20 or 285/35 ZR19, about 0.34 m unloaded). Check: 60 mph in 8th gives 1,543 rpm vs MotorTrend's measured 1,500 rpm.

shift_times.note: Not published. C/D: upshifts range 'from luxury-car mushy to rifle-bolt quick with almost no torque interruption' depending on Drivelogic. Suggest about 0.10-0.15 s torque dip at Drivelogic 3 (Sport+), 0.3-0.4 s in comfort.

torque_converter_lockup.value: Lock-up clutch fully engaged the moment the car has pulled away

torque_converter_stall_rpm.note: Not published. Launch holds about 2,700 rpm (BMAG_LC), so a full-throttle stall around 2,400-2,800 rpm is a reasonable estimate.

drivelogic.value: 3 shift programmes in D and 3 in M; paddles; holding left paddle with throttle drops to lowest possible gear; auto rev-matching on downshifts; in M mode no auto-upshift at the limiter

transmission_oil_cooler.value: Separate transmission oil cooler on Competition models

differential.value: Active M Differential: electronically controlled multi-plate limited-slip differential, variable 0-100% locking, networked with DSC
differential.note: BMW does not publish preload or lock values. Electric-motor-actuated clutch pack is assumed from the previous F80 system (A).

lock_behaviour_estimate.value: Model as a controlled clutch LSD: low preload (about 50-100 Nm) cruising, ramping toward full lock on power exit and under DSC-off drifting, partial lock on corner entry for stability

traction_control.value: DSC with M Dynamic Mode; slip control moved into the engine ECU (acts up to 10x more often); M Traction Control with 10 stages (with M Drive Professional)

m_xdrive.value: Electronically controlled multi-plate clutch in the transfer case; rear-only until rear grip limit; 4WD / 4WD Sport / 2WD (DSC off)

kerb_EU.note: EU: DIN + 75 kg driver/luggage. ADAC repeats 1,805 kg (EU).

kerb_measured_CD.note: 1,733 kg; car had carbon-ceramic brakes and M Driver's Package.

licensing_mass_ZA.note: South African licensing (tare) mass on the test sheet.

dry_weight.note: Not published. DIN minus fuel (59 L x 0.9 x 0.745 = 40 kg) gives about 1,690 kg; minus oil, coolant and ATF roughly 1,660 kg.

max_permissible.note: Max axle loads 1,080 kg front / 1,180 kg rear.

weight_distribution_factory.note: US spec table. The press kit's 'virtually 50:50' is marketing; factory and measured figures agree on 53/47.

xdrive_masses.note: US curb is F (BMW_US22XD); DIN/EU figures from BMW regional pages via search extracts (not opened); measured from MT_XD and CD_XD (Edition 50 Jahre with carbon buckets and CCB).

weight_savers.value: M Race Track Package about -25 kg; M Carbon bucket seats save 21 lb (9.5 kg); CFRP roof standard

width_with_mirrors.note: From the dimension drawing; US 81.4 in.

standard_EU_RWD.note: Forged M light-alloy wheels. US 2021 sheet lists the same as standard.

optional_and_xdrive_standard.note: Standard on M xDrive and in Canada; fitted to every magazine test car found. Load indices from CD_RWD.

value: Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 (track option, not offered in the US at launch)
oe_tyre_models.note: PS4S on C/D, MT, AMS and Citizen cars; P Zero PZ4 on the C/D xDrive car (CD_XD); Cup 2 option per BMW_CA and MT_FT.

standard.value: M Compound: front 380 mm vented discs, 6-piston fixed calipers; rear 370 mm vented discs, single-piston floating calipers with integrated parking brake

standard_disc_thickness.note: 380 x 36 and 370 x 24 from replacement-part listings.

carbon_ceramic_option.value: M Carbon ceramic: 400 mm front, 380 mm rear, gold calipers
carbon_ceramic_option.note: Front 400 x 38 mm per Turner note (P, indirect). C/D lists 15.7-in/15.0-in cross-drilled carbon-ceramic discs on its test cars.

brake_system.value: Integrated braking system (brake-by-wire module, electric actuator) with Comfort/Sport pedal-feel settings

braking_70_0_mph.note: 45.7 m, carbon-ceramic brakes, PS4S. xDrive: 153 ft (CD_XD).

braking_100_0_kmh.note: No European measurement found. Scaling MT's 60-0 (v^2) gives 33.3 m; scaling C/D's 70-0 gives 36.0 m. Mean decelerations 1.18 g (MT) and 1.09 g (C/D).

CdA.note: 0.33 x 2.34 from BMW's 'cd x A' entry.

downforce.note: Not published. BMW says the extended sills/aprons 'increase downforce in the underbody area' and the lip, Air Curtain flics and roof fins optimise aero balance (BMW_PK). For simulation assume near-zero net lift (small ClA, about 0.05-0.10 m^2 per axle).

active_aero.note: No moving aero devices are mentioned in the press kit.

front.value: Double-joint spring-strut axle, aluminium wishbones and torque arm, forged swivel bearing; large castor and kingpin angles; lowered roll centre

rear.value: Five-link axle in aluminium/steel, rear subframe rigidly bolted to the body

dampers.value: Adaptive M suspension: electronically controlled dampers, electromagnetic valves per wheel, Comfort / Sport / Sport Plus

spring_rates.note: Not published. From ride frequencies 1.6 Hz front / 1.8 Hz rear, EU mass 1,805 kg at 53.1/46.9, about 50 kg unsprung per corner.

cog_height.note: Not published. Typical for a lowered sedan with CFRP roof.

steering.value: Electric power steering with M Servotronic and variable sport ratio; Comfort/Sport modes

lock_to_lock_turns.note: AMS measured 2.25 turns; 370 mm wheel diameter (AMS).

top_speed_measured_gps.note: AutoTopNL GPS run with M Driver's Package (182 mph); from a search extract, page not loaded.

top_speed_unrestricted_estimate.note: Power balance: 330 kW at the wheels vs CdA 0.772 m^2 and 1.2% rolling resistance; would sit near 6,500 rpm in 7th.

CD_RWD_2021.note: Results omit 1-ft rollout (0.2 s). Michelin PS4S, carbon-ceramic brakes.

CITIZEN_2021.note: South Africa, 14 April 2021, 15 deg C, Michelin PS4S 275/35 R19 / 285/30 R20. Test altitude not stated.

estimated_0_200_kmh_measured_basis.note: Citizen 0-100 (3.64) + 100-200 (8.01) plus about 0.1 s for the shift overlap; quicker than BMW's 12.5 s, consistent with an underrated engine.

exhaust_layout.value: Per bank: 3-into-1 manifold cast into the turbine housing -> mono-scroll turbo -> close-coupled ceramic-monolith catalyst (one per bank) -> [EU/RoW only] underbody catalyst + gasoline particulate filter per branch -> centre silencer -> large rear silencer with two electric flaps in the outer tailpipes -> 4 tailpipes in two twin pairs, 100 mm each (Black Chrome on Competition). Dual-branch (cylinders 1-3 / 4-6) 'cylinder-dependent twin-pipe design'; the tailpipes are internally interconnected so gas always exits all four.
exhaust_layout.note: Component order from the S58 training manual (F97/F98, same engine family); dual-branch, rear silencer, quad 100 mm tips and flaps for G80 from BMW_PK. G80-specific centre-silencer details not seen.

flap_logic.value: Flaps are binary (fully open or closed, PWM 10% open / 90% closed). Closed at low rpm/low load for comfort and urban pass-by noise; open at high rpm/high load. SPORT / SPORT+ change timbre and intensity; the M Sound Control button keeps the flaps closed as long as possible and reduces ASD, overriding the drive mode.
flap_logic.note: Behaviour documented for S58 in F97/F98; G80 press kit describes the same SPORT/SPORT+/M Sound Control logic (BMW_PK).

turbo_sound_character.value: Two mono-scroll turbos with even 240-deg pulse spacing per branch; electric wastegates; no documented blow-off valve. Reviewers mainly note lag below about 2,750 rpm rather than turbo noise.
turbo_sound_character.note: No published description of turbo whistle found. Gap.

cd_interior_70mph.note: Steady 70 mph; four dB quieter than the previous M3 Competition.

cd_interior_idle.note: Not printed in the text; the comparison says the M3 was quieter than the Alfa at idle and 70 mph. Gap. AMS idle figure below.

eu_stationary_noise.note: From search extracts of BMW Malta/Malaysia technical-data pages for the M3 Competition (model year not visible). The 2024 G80 pages (Ireland/UK) show 91 dB(A) at 3,750 rpm. Low confidence: not read from a homologation document.

eu_pass_by_noise.note: ADAC 'Fahrgeraeusch' for M3 Competition Steptronic 07/22-05/24 (UN R51.03). BMW Malta/Malaysia extracts show 72 dB(A); 2024 Irish/UK extracts show 69 dB(A) for M xDrive.

active_sound_design.value: Fitted: engine orders are added through the audio system (ASD in the passenger compartment). It can be reduced with the M Sound Control button or switched off in a menu.
active_sound_design.note: C/D: 'At least you can turn off the auto-tune effect via a menu on the touchscreen' (CD_RWD). evo: 'augmented through the speakers' (EVO).

asd_share_estimate.value: About half of the in-cabin engine sound under load in SPORT/SPORT+ is speaker-generated; less in COMFORT or with M Sound Control active
asd_share_estimate.note: No published figure. Estimate from reviewer comments (C/D wanting more natural sound; evo calling it augmented but authentic). Use as a mixing guide only.

limiter_behaviour.value: Redline 7,200 rpm, limiter at about 7,250 rpm; in M mode the car holds the limiter rather than upshifting; expect a fast fuel/ignition-cut bounce.

overrun_pops_by_mode.value: Not documented by BMW. Stock EU cars sound muted outside (OPF). Expected: COMFORT/EFFICIENT - flaps mostly closed, little or no crackle; SPORT - light burble on lift-off from mid rpm; SPORT+ - most frequent burbles, still mild. M Sound Control suppresses them.
overrun_pops_by_mode.note: evo: 'fires with a satisfying burble' (start-up); a G80 owner reports the sound button 'cancels the burbles' (ASD_FORUM, anecdotal).

value.quote: The S58 motor fires with a satisfying burble.
It may be augmented through the speakers, but it's as authentic a sound as you could hope for.
the latest emission filters stuffed into the system result in a rather muted tone
it has a certain timbre and hollow resonance that suits its brutish appearance.
Maximum thrust results in 84 decibels of silky inline-six growl
we still wish BMW would let more of the engine's natural song into the cabin instead of boosting it through the audio system.
it suffers from the on-off nature of turbo lag
it isn't an indisputably wonderful straight-six.

reference_videos.note: Links only, nothing downloaded from YouTube. IDs were taken from embeds in the listed articles; titles were not checked on YouTube. No stock flyby or autobahn onboard link could be confirmed before the search budget ran out.

value.licence: CC BY 3.0 (YouTube Creative Commons option; Commons licence review still pending)
value.caveat: Aftermarket Fi Exhaust, not the stock system. Reference for engine orders and rev behaviour only, not for stock loudness or timbre. Confirm the licence review before any in-game use.

audio_engineer_notes.value: Fundamental firing frequency = rpm/20 Hz (3rd engine order); each exhaust branch carries the 1.5th order, so slight bank-to-bank differences add 1.5-order content. Rev range for loops: about 700 (idle) to 7,250 (limiter). Strong torque plateau 2,750-5,500 rpm means load-dependent timbre should change most around 2,000-3,000 rpm (boost onset).

body_style.value: Four-door notchback sports sedan; long bonnet, cab set back, short boot with integrated lip spoiler

engine_position.value: Front, longitudinal inline-6 roughly over and behind the front axle line

method.value: Proportions measured on BMW's orthographic side drawing (pixel scale 3.71 mm/px, heights normalised to the 1,433 mm roof); cross-checked by eye against a CC BY-SA 4.0 Commons photo (front three-quarter, not a pure profile; no pure profile was found among 40 sampled Commons files)

windscreen_base_fraction.note: About 1.50 m from the nose, height about 0.99 m (cowl).

windscreen_top_fraction.note: Roof header about 2.35 m from the nose at about 1.40 m.

roof_peak_fraction.note: About 2.82 m from the nose, near the B-pillar. Roof stays within 10 mm of peak from 0.53 to 0.68.

roof_height.note: A small shark-fin antenna sits at about 0.71 L.

rear_screen_fractions.note: Rear screen runs from the roof end (about 1.39 m high) down to the boot lid (about 1.07 m).

silhouette_heights.unit: [fraction of length from front, top-of-body height mm]
silhouette_heights.note: Upper silhouette traced from the drawing; last point is the drop at the tail face.

nose_shape.value: Tall, blunt, near-vertical front face dominated by a very large vertical twin-kidney grille; bonnet top about 0.64 m at the nose rising to about 0.99 m at the cowl; deep front apron with outer vertical air-curtain intakes

tail_shape.value: Short notchback deck ending in a body-colour or gloss-black lip spoiler at about 1.04 m; near-vertical tail face; black diffuser with four 100 mm tips in two pairs

wheel_size_visual.value: Tyre outer diameter about 0.68 m front and rear

simulated_mass_with_driver.note: EU unladen weight already includes 75 kg driver/luggage; equals DIN 1,730 + 75.

performance_targets.note: Magazine tests run about 0.3 s quicker to 100 km/h (Citizen 3.64 s).
